--!strict
-- Deterministic pure harness. No external packages or runtime dependencies.
return function(ResourceMath: any, cases: any)
	local results = { run = 0, passed = 0, failed = 0, cases = {} }
	local context = {}
	function context.test(name: string, fn: () -> ())
		results.run += 1
		local ok, err = pcall(fn)
		local status = if ok then "PASS" else "FAIL"
		if ok then results.passed += 1 else results.failed += 1 end
		table.insert(results.cases, { name = name, status = status, error = if ok then "" else tostring(err) })
		print(string.format("[STAGE04][%s] %s%s", status, name, if ok then "" else " | " .. tostring(err)))
	end
	local ok, err = pcall(cases, ResourceMath, context)
	if not ok then context.test("suite registration", function() error(tostring(err)) end) end
	print(string.format("[STAGE04][SUMMARY] %d run, %d passed, %d failed", results.run, results.passed, results.failed))
	return results
end

--!strict
-- Contract tests; same injected-module convention as existing Economy.spec.
return function(ResourceMath: any, t: any)
	local function near(actual: number, expected: number)
		assert(actual == actual and math.abs(actual - expected) <= 1e-6,
			string.format("expected %.12g, got %.12g", expected, actual))
	end
	local function rejects(value: any)
		local valid, reason = ResourceMath.ValidateDropTable(value)
		assert(valid == false and type(reason) == "string")
		assert(not pcall(ResourceMath.CalculateExpectedValue, value), "invalid drops must raise")
	end
	local zones = {
		{ name = "Whispering Meadows", weights = {70, 25, 5}, prices = {5, 12, 30}, terms = {3.5, 3, 1.5}, ev = 8, count = 9, route = 72 },
		{ name = "Crystal Ruins", weights = {55, 40, 5}, prices = {12, 30, 80}, terms = {6.6, 12, 4}, ev = 22.6, count = 7, route = 158.2 },
		{ name = "Storm Temple", weights = {60, 38, 2}, prices = {30, 80, 220}, terms = {18, 30.4, 4.4}, ev = 52.8, count = 4, route = 211.2 },
	}
	for _, zone in ipairs(zones) do
		local drops = {}
		for i, weight in ipairs(zone.weights) do
			drops[i] = { probability = weight / 100, price = zone.prices[i] }
			-- Independent hand-derived contribution of each drop.
			t.test(zone.name .. " contribution " .. i, function()
				near(drops[i].probability * drops[i].price, zone.terms[i])
			end)
		end
		-- Check probabilities without invoking production validation.
		t.test(zone.name .. " probability sum", function()
			local sum = 0
			for _, row in ipairs(drops) do sum += row.probability end
			near(sum, 1)
			assert(ResourceMath.ValidateDropTable(drops))
		end)
		-- Expected value oracle uses 100 equally likely outcomes, not weighted multiplication.
		t.test(zone.name .. " independent expectation", function()
			local outcomeSum, outcomeCount = 0, 0
			for i, weight in ipairs(zone.weights) do
				for _ = 1, weight do
					outcomeSum += zone.prices[i]
					outcomeCount += 1
				end
			end
			assert(outcomeCount == 100)
			near(outcomeSum / outcomeCount, zone.ev)
			near(ResourceMath.CalculateExpectedValue(drops), outcomeSum / outcomeCount)
		end)
		-- Route oracle uses repeated addition and the user-confirmed route total.
		t.test(zone.name .. " route", function()
			local reference = 0
			for _ = 1, zone.count do reference += zone.ev end
			near(reference, zone.route)
			near(ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue(ResourceMath.CalculateExpectedValue(drops), zone.count), zone.route)
		end)
	end

	-- Each malformed fixture is independently rejected by validation and calculation.
	local invalid: { { name: string, value: any } } = {
		{ name = "empty drops", value = {} },
		{ name = "sum above one", value = {{probability = 1.1, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "sum below one", value = {{probability = 0.9, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "negative price", value = {{probability = 1, price = -1}} },
		{ name = "negative probability", value = {{probability = -0.1, price = 1}, {probability = 1.1, price = 1}} },
		{ name = "wrong container type", value = "drops" },
		{ name = "wrong row type", value = {5} },
		{ name = "wrong probability type", value = {{probability = "1", price = 5}} },
		{ name = "wrong price type", value = {{probability = 1, price = "5"}} },
		{ name = "missing probability", value = {{price = 5}} },
		{ name = "missing price", value = {{probability = 1}} },
		{ name = "NaN probability", value = {{probability = 0/0, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "NaN price", value = {{probability = 1, price = 0/0}} },
		{ name = "infinite probability", value = {{probability = math.huge, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "infinite price", value = {{probability = 1, price = math.huge}} },
		{ name = "negative infinity", value = {{probability = 1, price = -math.huge}} },
		{ name = "sparse array", value = {[1] = {probability = 0.5, price = 5}, [3] = {probability = 0.5, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "dictionary keys", value = {drop = {probability = 1, price = 5}} },
		{ name = "outside tolerance", value = {{probability = 1 + 2e-6, price = 5}} },
	}
	for _, fixture in ipairs(invalid) do
		t.test(fixture.name, function() rejects(fixture.value) end)
	end
	-- Nil must not be lost from an array of fixtures.
	t.test("nil drops", function() rejects(nil) end)
	-- Small input rounding errors are accepted without renormalizing probabilities.
	t.test("inside tolerance", function()
		assert(ResourceMath.ValidateDropTable({{probability = 1 + 0.5e-6, price = 5}}))
	end)
	-- Zero probability and zero prices are valid.
	t.test("zero price and probability", function()
		near(ResourceMath.CalculateExpectedValue({{probability=0,price=100},{probability=1,price=0}}), 0)
	end)
	-- Zero gathers costs zero.
	t.test("zero gathers", function() near(ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue(8, 0), 0) end)
	-- Invalid route inputs cannot produce plausible numeric answers.
	for _, value in ipairs({-1, 0.5, math.huge, 0/0, "9"}) do
		t.test("invalid count " .. tostring(value), function()
			assert(not pcall(ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue, 8, value))
		end)
	end
	-- Invalid expected values must fail even with a valid count.
	for _, value in ipairs({-1, math.huge, 0/0, "8"}) do
		t.test("invalid expectation " .. tostring(value), function()
			assert(not pcall(ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue, value, 9))
		end)
	end
	-- Finite operands can still overflow.
	t.test("route overflow", function() assert(not pcall(ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue, 1e308, 10)) end)
end

--!strict
-- Pure arithmetic only. No currency, inventory, persistence or network writes.
local ResourceMath = {}
local EPSILON = 0.000001

local function finite(value: any): boolean
	return type(value) == "number" and value == value and math.abs(value) < math.huge
end

-- Contract: a nonempty dense array of {probability: number, price: number}.
-- Invalid input returns false and a diagnostic; calculations raise on invalid input.
function ResourceMath.ValidateDropTable(drops: any): (boolean, string?)
	if type(drops) ~= "table" then
		return false, "drops must be an array"
	end
	local count, maximum, total = 0, 0, 0
	for key, row in pairs(drops) do
		if type(key) ~= "number" or not finite(key) or key < 1 or key % 1 ~= 0 then
			return false, "drops must have positive integer array keys"
		end
		count += 1
		maximum = math.max(maximum, key)
		if type(row) ~= "table" then
			return false, "each drop must be a record"
		end
		local record = row :: {[string]: any}
		local probability, price = record.probability, record.price
		if type(probability) ~= "number" or not finite(probability) or probability < 0 then
			return false, "probability must be finite and nonnegative"
		end
		if type(price) ~= "number" or not finite(price) or price < 0 then
			return false, "price must be finite and nonnegative"
		end
		total += probability
	end
	if count == 0 then
		return false, "drops must not be empty"
	end
	if maximum ~= count then
		return false, "drops must not contain holes"
	end
	if not finite(total) or math.abs(total - 1) > EPSILON then
		return false, "probabilities must sum to 1 within 0.000001"
	end
	return true, nil
end

function ResourceMath.CalculateExpectedValue(drops: any): number
	local valid, reason = ResourceMath.ValidateDropTable(drops)
	assert(valid, reason)
	local total = 0
	for _, row in ipairs(drops) do
		total += row.probability * row.price
	end
	assert(finite(total), "expected value overflow")
	return total
end

function ResourceMath.CalculateRouteValue(expectedValue: any, count: any): number
	assert(finite(expectedValue) and expectedValue >= 0, "expectedValue must be finite and nonnegative")
	assert(finite(count) and count >= 0 and count % 1 == 0, "count must be a finite nonnegative integer")
	local result = expectedValue * count
	assert(finite(result), "route value overflow")
	return result
end

return ResourceMath

--!strict
local Economy = {}
function Economy.roll(drops, roll: number): string
 assert(roll >= 0 and roll < 100, 'roll outside [0,100)')
 local sum = 0
 for _, row in drops do sum += row[2]; if roll < sum then return row[1] end end
 error('invalid drop table')
end
function Economy.sellValue(config, inventory): number
 local sum = 0
 for id, count in inventory do
  assert(config.items[id] and count >= 0 and count % 1 == 0, 'invalid inventory')
  sum += config.items[id].price * count
 end
 return sum
end
function Economy.upgrade(config, profile): boolean
 local cost = config.upgrades[profile.level]
 if not cost or profile.coins < cost.coins then return false end
 for id,n in cost.items do if (profile.inventory[id] or 0) < n then return false end end
 profile.coins -= cost.coins
 for id,n in cost.items do profile.inventory[id] -= n end
 profile.level += 1
 return true
end
return Economy

local Players=game:GetService('Players')

local Economy=require(shared.Shared.Economy)
local world=require(script.Parent.Services.World).build()
local remote=Instance.new('RemoteEvent');remote.Name='State';remote.Parent=shared
local profiles={};local random=Random.new()
local function publish(player,p,message)
 player:SetAttribute('SkyCoins',p.coins);player:SetAttribute('SkyHeart',p.level)
 local count=0;for _,n in p.inventory do count+=n end;player:SetAttribute('BagCount',count)
 remote:FireClient(player,{coins=p.coins,level=p.level,inventory=p.inventory,message=message})
end
local function ready(player,target)
 local p=profiles[player];local char=player.Character;local root=char and char:FindFirstChild('HumanoidRootPart');local h=char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
 if not p or not root or not h or h.Health<=0 or (root.Position-target.Position).Magnitude>config.prototype.gatherDistance then return nil end
 local now=os.clock();if now-p.last<config.prototype.requestInterval then return nil end;p.last=now;return p
end
local function joined(player) local p={coins=0,level=1,inventory={},nodes={},last=-math.huge};profiles[player]=p;task.defer(function() player.RespawnLocation=world.model.AetherSpawn end);publish(player,p,'Welcome to SKYKEEPERS') end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(joined);Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) profiles[p]=nil end)
for _,p in Players:GetPlayers() do joined(p) end
for id,node in world.nodes do node.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
 local p=ready(player,node);if not p then return end
 local now=os.clock();if p.nodes[id] and now-p.nodes[id]<config.prototype.nodeCooldown then publish(player,p,'This node is recharging');return end
 local total=0;for _,n in p.inventory do total+=n end;if total>=config.prototype.inventoryCap then return end
 local item=Economy.roll(config.zones.WhisperingMeadows.drops,random:NextNumber()*100)
 p.nodes[id]=now;p.inventory[item]=(p.inventory[item] or 0)+1;publish(player,p,'Found '..item..' ['..config.items[item].rarity..']')
end) end
world.merchant.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
 local p=ready(player,world.merchant);if not p then return end
 local value=Economy.sellValue(config,p.inventory);p.inventory={};p.coins+=value;publish(player,p,'Sold for '..value..' SC')
end)
world.heart.ProximityPrompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
 local p=ready(player,world.heart);if not p then return end
 publish(player,p,Economy.upgrade(config,p) and 'Sky Heart upgraded!' or 'Need coins and materials; keep some resources for upgrades')
end)
